impact.why_not_5: A careful replication harness, but it shows only that existing instruments miss silent coordination; it never demonstrates an instrument or audit that catches it, so the theory of change stays hypothetical.
impact.one_change_for_5: K3: a price-screen authority arm on Sonnet and no-channel Haiku, with false-positive rate on scripted Nash players, showing what an auditor can actually reach.
impact.feasibility_why: New regime plus screen calibration is roughly ten hours and about 20 USD; doable solo if scoped to two arms and pre-registered as an amendment.

execution.why_not_5: Four pool sessions per regime, two for Sonnet without a no-channel baseline, one provider, told-only points: validation is unusually good, but the headline inferences rest on thin clusters.
execution.one_change_for_5: K2 plus K1: Sonnet on 4 pools with its no-channel arm and Haiku core regimes at 8 pools with a permutation test over pools.
execution.feasibility_why: About 19 USD and parallel runs fit; a second provider, the missing piece for a true 5, depends on uncertain GPU credits.

presentation.why_not_5: Clear structure, but the running text is a wall of paired numbers, Table 3 columns break mid-word, Figure 1 labels overlap, and the page-1 title differs from the stated one.
presentation.one_change_for_5: K6: one claim per paragraph with numbers moved to tables, repaired Table 3 widths, legible Figure 1 annotations, and a testbed-first abstract.
presentation.feasibility_why: Pure editing and plotting work, no API cost, about four hours including a final proofread of the rendered PDF.

K1.risk_note: Result 3 may still miss the interval rule; new pools shift every number and force a full text refresh.

K2.risk_note: If Sonnet holds the same price without a channel, the prohibition story weakens; still informative, but needs rewriting.

K3.risk_note: New regime code and screen threshold choice could look tuned post hoc; must be pre-registered before running.

K4.risk_note: Stated reasons may be unfaithful rationalisations; an LLM judge adds a validity question reviewers will raise.

K5.risk_note: Account unlock uncertain; open-model setup, JSON compliance and positive control can eat the whole day.

K6.risk_note: Trimming numbers could drop the baseline next to a claim; keep each comparison intact.

package.why: K2 supplies the no-channel baseline K3 needs; K3 turns diagnosis into an auditable instrument; K4 grounds mechanisms; K6 is cheap. About 25 hours, 38 USD. K5 too risky, K1 marginal.

five_realistic.why: Impact reaches 5 only if the screen arm reaches silent coordination with a low false-positive rate. Execution stays capped by one provider and small clusters. Presentation needs a disciplined rewrite, not new data.

stable_optimum: 4/4/4: presentation rises with K6, execution firms up with K2 and K4, and impact reaches 5 only if K3 cleanly shows a screen catching silent coordination.
